::: {#rem-connective-notation}
#### Notation, and the inclusive "or"

Some textbooks write $\sim P$ for $\neg P$.
Programming languages spell the same three connectives as words or symbols:
Racket writes `(not p)`, `(and p q)` and `(or p q)`,
and Java and C write `!p`, `p && q` and `p || q`.

In everyday English, "soup or salad" often means one but not both.
The logical "or" always allows both,
as the first row of its truth table shows.

:::
